ana: Found a case where snapshot uploads are missing tenant tags in audit-store after an RBAC change rolled yesterday.
tom: which RBAC change?
ana: we tightened restore-service IAM role to assume a short-lived role via token-exchange. Lina repro'd it.
lina: sequence I saw: service requested KMS grant (context includes tenant_id), then role swap happened, s3 PutObject succeeded but audit-emitter had no tenant and wrote empty tags.
kms-bot: grant recorded: id=g-2026abc key=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/abcd principal=svc-restore context={tenant_id:acct-55,request:r-21}
ana: tl;dr: KMS context good, object encrypted, but audit-store missing tenant -> risk: misindexed snapshots and downstream ACLs rely on tags.
tom: severity? potential for cross-tenant access?
ana: likely low for decryption because grants ephemeral, but medium for governance and billing+restore confusion. mark P2.
ops-bot: ticket INC-20260329-012 created, assigned @encops @restore-team
lina: quick mitigations: 1) revert RBAC token-exchange roll temporarily 2) patch audit-emitter to fetch tenant from KMS grant if local context absent 3) add preflight assert: fail upload if tenant tag missing.
tom: agree. also add a backfill job to reconcile objects without tenant tags by joining KMS grant logs.
ana: I'll run a 48h scan and share CSV. after fixes, run a controlled restore of a few snapshots to verify audit continuity.
lina: long-term: make request-scoped tenant binding immutable for the duration of operation and add e2e test covering role swap and credential rotation.
ana: thanks; keeping updates short here. escalate if cross-tenant reads detected. :lock:
